andhra-pradesh.name: Andhra Pradesh
andhra-pradesh.description: Sacred coastal state home to the Tirumala Venkateswara shrine, Buddhist stupas of Amaravati, and Lepakshi hanging pillar marvel.

arunachal-pradesh.name: Arunachal Pradesh
arunachal-pradesh.description: Arunachal Pradesh, known as the Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains, is India easternmost state, characterized by dramatic Himalayan river valleys, ancient Mahayana Buddhist gompas, and pristine biodiversity hotspots.

assam.name: Assam
assam.description: Brahmaputra valley home to Kaziranga one-horned rhinos, Majuli river island, Kamakhya temple, and lush tea gardens.

bihar.name: Bihar
bihar.description: Cradle of ancient empires (Maurya and Gupta), enlightenment grounds of Gautama Buddha, and birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh.

chhattisgarh.name: Chhattisgarh
chhattisgarh.description: Green heartland of India boasting Chitrakote Horseshoe Falls, ancient Sirpur Buddhist brick monuments, and Bastar tribal arts.

goa.name: Goa
goa.description: Coastal jewel celebrated for UNESCO Churches of Old Goa, golden sandy beaches, Portuguese architecture, and spice plantations.

gujarat.name: Gujarat
gujarat.description: Land of Legends featuring Ahmedabad World Heritage City, Rani ki Vav stepwell, Champaner, Somnath, and Asiatic Lions of Gir.

haryana.name: Haryana
haryana.description: Vedic heartland of the epic Mahabharata, ancient Harappan archaeological mounds at Rakhigarhi, and Pinjore Mughal gardens.

himachal-pradesh.name: Himachal Pradesh
himachal-pradesh.description: Himachal Pradesh is a northern Indian Himalayan state renowned for high-altitude ecosystems, historic Buddhist monasteries, wooden pagoda temples, and historic hill stations.

jharkhand.name: Jharkhand
jharkhand.description: Land of Forests and waterfalls, sacred Baidyanath Jyotirlinga at Deoghar, Parasnath Jain pilgrimage, and tribal cultural heritage.

karnataka.name: Karnataka
karnataka.description: One State Many Worlds featuring UNESCO Vijayanagara ruins at Hampi, Hoysala Sacred Ensembles, and Badami Chalukya cave temples.

kerala.name: Kerala
kerala.description: God's Own Country featuring palm-fringed backwaters of Alappuzha, Munnar tea hills, historic Fort Kochi, and Kathakali traditions.

madhya-pradesh.name: Madhya Pradesh
madhya-pradesh.description: The Heart of India with three UNESCO sites: Khajuraho temples, Sanchi Buddhist stupas, and Bhimbetka rock shelters.

maharashtra.name: Maharashtra
maharashtra.description: Gateway to India with 5 UNESCO World Heritage sites: Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta Caves, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, and Victorian Ensembles.

manipur.name: Manipur
manipur.description: Jeweled land featuring Loktak Lake with floating phumdis, Keibul Lamjao Sangai deer park, and sacred Kangla Fort.

meghalaya.name: Meghalaya
meghalaya.description: Abode of Clouds, renowned for living root bridges, Cherrapunjee waterfalls, clean village Mawlynnong, and Khasi culture.

mizoram.name: Mizoram
mizoram.description: Land of Rolling Hills and bamboo forests, known for its ridge-top capital Aizawl, Cheraw bamboo dance, and pristine lakes.

nagaland.name: Nagaland
nagaland.description: Land of Festivals, celebrated for the Hornbill Festival, 16 indigenous warrior tribes, WWII Kohima War Cemetery, and Dzukou Valley.

odisha.name: Odisha
odisha.description: Soul of Incredible India featuring Konark Sun Temple (UNESCO), Puri Jagannath shrine, Chilika lagoon, and Kalinga architecture.

punjab.name: Punjab
punjab.description: Punjab, the land of five rivers, is the cradle of Sikh heritage and a vibrant agricultural hub in northwest India, known for historic gurdwaras, majestic palaces, martial traditions, and rich culinary arts.

rajasthan.name: Rajasthan
rajasthan.description: Rajasthan, the Land of Kings, showcases royal Rajput architecture, desert expanses, UNESCO World Heritage Hill Forts, intricately painted havelis, wildlife sanctuaries, and vibrant handicrafts.

sikkim.name: Sikkim
sikkim.description: Himalayan wonderland crowned by Mt. Khangchendzonga (UNESCO Mixed World Heritage), Buddhist monasteries, and alpine lakes.

tamil-nadu.name: Tamil Nadu
tamil-nadu.description: Land of Living Chola Temples (UNESCO), soaring Dravidian gopurams of Madurai, Shore Temple of Mamallapuram, and Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

telangana.name: Telangana
telangana.description: City of Pearls and Nizams, home to Charminar, Golconda Fort, and UNESCO World Heritage Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple.

tripura.name: Tripura
tripura.description: Historic kingdom featuring the lakeside Neermahal palace, Ujjayanta Palace, and colossal 7th-9th century rock reliefs at Unakoti.

uttar-pradesh.name: Uttar Pradesh
uttar-pradesh.description: Uttar Pradesh, situated in the fertile Indo-Gangetic plain, is a foundational center of Indian classical civilization, home to holy rivers Ganga and Yamuna, world-renowned Mughal and Awadhi monuments, and sacred pilgrimage centers.

uttarakhand.name: Uttarakhand
uttarakhand.description: Land of Gods (Devbhoomi), sacred Char Dham Himalayan pilgrimage, Yoga capital Rishikesh, and Nanda Devi UNESCO reserve.

west-bengal.name: West Bengal
west-bengal.description: Cultural capital of India featuring Victoria Memorial, UNESCO Sundarbans, Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, and terracotta Bishnupur.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.description: Archipelago in the Bay of Bengal with historic Cellular Jail, pristine coral reefs, and limestone caves of Baratang.

chandigarh.name: Chandigarh
chandigarh.description: Planned modernist city designed by Le Corbusier, featuring the UNESCO Capitol Complex and Sukhna Lake.

dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.description: Coastal Portuguese heritage territory featuring sea-facing fortress walls, baroque churches, and pristine beaches of Diu.

delhi.name: Delhi
delhi.description: India's historic national capital featuring iconic Mughal citadels, colonial boulevards, and three UNESCO World Heritage complexes.

jammu-and-kashmir.name: Jammu and Kashmir
jammu-and-kashmir.description: Paradise on Earth, celebrated for Dal Lake shikaras, Mughal gardens, Vaishno Devi shrine, and alpine meadows of Gulmarg.

ladakh.name: Ladakh
ladakh.description: High-altitude desert trans-Himalaya featuring Buddhist gompas, Pangong Tso azure waters, and high mountain passes.

lakshadweep.name: Lakshadweep
lakshadweep.description: Emerald coral atolls in the Arabian Sea with crystal lagoons, marine biodiversity, and traditional coir crafts.

puducherry.name: Puducherry
puducherry.description: French Riviera of the East, featuring tree-lined colonial boulevards in White Town, Sri Aurobindo Ashram, and universal city Auroville.

amaravati.name: Amaravati
amaravati.description: Ancient riverbank Buddhist site boasting the Great Mahachaitya stupa ruins, museums, and seat of Andhra Pradesh administration.

anantapur.name: Anantapur
anantapur.description: Rayalaseema historic district home to Gooty Fort, clock tower heritage, and gateway to the hanging pillars of Lepakshi.

tirupati.name: Tirupati
tirupati.description: World-renowned pilgrimage destination resting at the foothills of the holy Tirumala hills, home to Sri Venkateswara Swamy shrine.

visakhapatnam.name: Visakhapatnam
visakhapatnam.description: Cosmopolitan coastal port city with golden beaches, INS Kursura submarine museum, Kailasagiri hill views, and Borra Caves.

tawang.name: Tawang
tawang.description: Tawang is situated in the northwestern corner of Arunachal Pradesh at an elevation of 3,048 meters. It is famous for Tawang Monastery (the largest in India and second largest in the world), Sela Pass, and picturesque high-altitude alpine lakes.

bomdila.name: Bomdila
bomdila.description: Picturesque hill town with panoramic vistas of snow-capped Gorichen and Kangto peaks, Buddhist gompas, and apple orchards.

itanagar.name: Itanagar
itanagar.description: State capital guarded by the 14th-century irregular brick Ita Fort, serene Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi), and Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum.

mechuka.name: Mechuka
mechuka.description: Pristine high-altitude valley bordered by snow peaks, 400-year-old Samten Yongcha gompa, Yargyapchu river, and Memba tribal villages.

namsai.name: Namsai
namsai.description: Spiritual haven famed for the glittering Burmese-style Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham) at Tengapani and Tai Khamti Buddhist festivals.

pasighat.name: Pasighat
pasighat.description: Historic British-era settlement nestled where the roaring Siang river meets the plains, gateway to whitewater rafting expeditions.

ziro.name: Ziro
ziro.description: UNESCO-tentative valley renowned for unique sustainable paddy-cum-fish agro-systems, sacred Tarin groves, and annual outdoor Ziro Music Festival.

dibrugarh.name: Dibrugarh
dibrugarh.description: Tea City of India nestled on the Brahmaputra, gateway to lush colonial tea estates, river cruises, and Dehing Patkai rainforest.

guwahati.name: Guwahati
guwahati.description: Gateway to Northeast India, home to the sacred Kamakhya Shakti Peetha, Umananda peacock river island, and Brahmaputra ropeway.

jorhat.name: Jorhat
jorhat.description: Historical cultural center, home to Tocklai Tea Research Institute, sprawling tea bungalows, and main ferry launch point for Majuli.

arrah.name: Arrah
arrah.description: Historic town famed for 1857 Indian Uprising hero Veer Kunwar Singh fort, Jagdishpur heritage, and Arrah House colonial battleground.

gaya.name: Gaya
gaya.description: Ancient spiritual sanctum including the Vishnupad Temple on the Falgu river and UNESCO World Heritage Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya.

nalanda.name: Nalanda
nalanda.description: UNESCO World Heritage 5th-century Buddhist university archaeological ruins, multimedia museum, and neighboring Magadha capital Rajgir.

patna.name: Patna
patna.description: Ancient Mauryan capital Pataliputra, home to Takht Sri Patna Sahib, historic Golghar beehive granary, and world-class Bihar Museum.

dantewada.name: Dantewada
dantewada.description: Ancient sacred realm situated at the confluence of Shankhini and Dhankini rivers, celebrated for the 14th-century Danteshwari Shakti Peetha.

jagdalpur.name: Jagdalpur
jagdalpur.description: Tourism capital of Bastar featuring the Niagara of India Chitrakote Falls, Tirathgarh cascades, Kotumsar dripstone caves, and Bastar crafts.

raipur.name: Raipur
raipur.description: State capital on the Mahanadi basin featuring Purkhouti Muktangan cultural park, Swami Vivekananda Sarovar, and gateway to Sirpur.

rajnandgaon.name: Rajnandgaon
rajnandgaon.description: Historic princely seat known for Dongargarh Bambleshwari hilltop temple reached by ropeway, royal palaces, and peace-pagoda monuments.

goa.name: Goa
goa.description: Coastal paradise famed for UNESCO Churches of Old Goa, Baroque basilicas, Latin Quarters of Fontainhas, coastal forts, and sandy beaches.

ahmedabad.name: Ahmedabad
ahmedabad.description: India's first UNESCO World Heritage City, home to Sabarmati Ashram, Sidi Saiyyed Mosque filigree stone latticework, and Adalaj Stepwell.

bhavnagar.name: Bhavnagar
bhavnagar.description: Historic maritime kingdom with Nilambag Palace, Takhteshwar Temple hill, and gateway to the 800+ marble Jain temples of Palitana.

champaner.name: Champaner
champaner.description: UNESCO World Heritage archaeological park combining pre-Mughal Islamic architecture, stepwells, mosques, and Kalika Mata hilltop shrine.

dwarka.name: Dwarka
dwarka.description: Sacred Char Dham coastal pilgrimage center on the Arabian Sea, home to the multi-tiered 72-pillar Dwarkadhish temple of Lord Krishna.

gandhinagar.name: Gandhinagar
gandhinagar.description: Green capital city planned on the Sabarmati river, home to the colossal carved sandstone Akshardham temple complex and Dandi Kutir museum.

gir-somnath.name: Gir Somnath
gir-somnath.description: First of the twelve holy Jyotirlinga shrines facing the Arabian Sea, alongside the dry-deciduous forest kingdom of the Asiatic Lions in Gir.

jamnagar.name: Jamnagar
jamnagar.description: Jewel of Kathiawar famed for Lakhota Palace inside a lake, Khijadiya Bird Sanctuary, Marine National Park coral reefs, and Bandhani silk.

kutch.name: Kutch
kutch.description: Vast salt marsh wilderness hosting the world-famous Rann Utsav, Dholavira UNESCO Harappan archaeological site, and vibrant Rogan embroidery.

surat.name: Surat
surat.description: Diamond City and historic Mughal trading port on the Tapi river, famous for textile markets, Dutch and British colonial cemeteries, and food.

vadodara.name: Vadodara
vadodara.description: Cultural capital of Gujarat home to the majestic 700-acre Laxmi Vilas Palace (4 times size of Buckingham), museums, and Sayaji Baug.

faridabad.name: Faridabad
faridabad.description: Historic industrial city home to 10th-century Surajkund sun pool stepwell amphitheatre, annual International Crafts Mela, and Raja Nahar Singh Palace.

gurugram.name: Gurugram
gurugram.description: Millennium City combining futuristic cyber hubs with heritage Sheesh Mahal at Farrukhnagar, Sultanpur Bird Sanctuary, and Sheetla Mata temple.

hisar.name: Hisar
hisar.description: Historical fortified city founded in 1354 by Firoz Shah Tughlaq featuring Firoz Shah Palace complex, Lat Ki Masjid, and Harappan Rakhigarhi.

kurukshetra.name: Kurukshetra
kurukshetra.description: Sacred cradle of the Bhagavad Gita, huge Brahma Sarovar holy tank, Jyotisar banyan tree enlightenment site, and Sheikh Chilli tomb.

yamunanagar.name: Yamunanagar
yamunanagar.description: Foothill district featuring Kalesar National Park sal forests, Buddhist stupa at Chaneti, and ancient Sugh archaeological mound.

shimla.name: Shimla
shimla.description: Shimla is the capital city of Himachal Pradesh, situated along a ridge at an average elevation of 2,205 meters. It retains significant British colonial heritage including the Viceregal Lodge, Christ Church, and the UNESCO-inscribed Kalka-Shimla mountain railway.

manali.name: Manali
manali.description: Manali is situated along the Beas River at 2,050 meters elevation in Kullu district. Known for deodar forests, ancient wooden pagodas, and adventure expeditions across Solang and the Atal Tunnel.

spiti-valley.name: Spiti Valley
spiti-valley.description: Spiti Valley is an expansive high-altitude cold desert valley located at an average altitude of 3,800 meters in Lahaul and Spiti district. It is famous for thousand-year-old Tibetan Buddhist monasteries including Tabo and Key, fossil villages, and Chandratal wetland.

dharamshala.name: Dharamshala
dharamshala.description: Dharamshala is situated on the lower slopes of the Dhauladhar range. It is divided into lower Dharamshala and upper McLeod Ganj, serving as the residence of the 14th Dalai Lama and headquarters of Tibetan culture in exile.

kangra.name: Kangra
kangra.description: Kangra was the capital of the Katoch dynasty, one of the oldest surviving royal dynasties in the world. The town is famous for Kangra Fort, the Bajreshwari Devi Shaktipeeth, and close proximity to the 8th-century Masrur Rock Cut Temples.

kullu.name: Kullu
kullu.description: Kullu is situated on the banks of the Beas River at 1,278 meters elevation. It serves as the gateway to the Great Himalayan National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site), Parvati Valley, and traditional handloom shawls.

bilaspur.name: Bilaspur
bilaspur.description: Cultural and railway hub featuring the 11th-century Ratanpur Mahamaya Temple, Malhar archaeological remains, and Achanakmar Tiger Reserve.

reckong-peo.name: Reckong Peo
reckong-peo.description: Headquarters of Kinnaur offering spellbinding views of the sacred Kinnaur Kailash peak, apple orchards, and Kalpa heritage village.

deoghar.name: Deoghar
deoghar.description: Abode of the Gods, home to Baba Baidyanath Jyotirlinga temple complex drawing millions of Kanwariya pilgrims, Naulakha temple, and Trikut Pahar.

jamshedpur.name: Jamshedpur
jamshedpur.description: The Steel City founded by Jamsetji Tata, an impeccably planned green oasis with Jubilee Park, Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary, and Dimna Lake.

ranchi.name: Ranchi
ranchi.description: City of Waterfalls (Hundru, Jonha, Dassam), Pahari Mandir hilltop, Tagore Hill cultural retreat, and tribal heritage museums.

badami.name: Badami
badami.description: Regal capital of the early Chalukyas, renowned for four monolithic rock-cut cave temples carved into red sandstone cliffs above Agastya Lake.

bagalkote.name: Bagalkote
bagalkote.description: Northern Karnataka cultural hub on the Ghataprabha River, gateway to the temple architecture centers of Aihole and Pattadakal (UNESCO).

bengaluru.name: Bengaluru
bengaluru.description: Silicon Valley of India combining modern technology with heritage Lalbagh Botanical Gardens, Tudor-style Bangalore Palace, and Tipu Sultan Summer Palace.

dharwad.name: Dharwad
dharwad.description: Twin cultural capital with Hubli, celebrated as cradle of Hindustani classical music legends (Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal) and Dharwad Peda.

hampi.name: Hampi
hampi.description: UNESCO World Heritage monument complex spanning 4,100 hectares of ruins of the medieval Vijayanagara Empire, Stone Chariot, and Virupaksha Temple.

mangaluru.name: Mangaluru
mangaluru.description: Coastal port city famed for 10th-century Kadri Manjunatha temple bronze idols, St. Aloysius Chapel frescoes, Panambur beach, and coastal cuisine.

mysuru.name: Mysuru
mysuru.description: Cultural Capital of Karnataka home to the Indo-Saracenic Mysore Palace illuminated by 100,000 bulbs, Chamundi Hill, and Mysore Dasara.

udupi.name: Udupi
udupi.description: Spiritual destination centered on the 13th-century Sri Krishna Matha founded by Madhvacharya with Kanakana Kindi window, Malpe beach, and St. Mary Island.

vijayapura.name: Vijayapura
vijayapura.description: Historic Adil Shahi capital famed for the colossal dome of Gol Gumbaz (second largest dome in the world) with acoustic Whispering Gallery and Ibrahim Rauza.

alappuzha.name: Alappuzha
alappuzha.description: Venice of the East, heart of Kerala backwaters with houseboats cruising Vembanad Lake, Alappuzha beach lighthouse, and Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race.

kochi.name: Kochi
kochi.description: Queen of the Arabian Sea featuring cantilevered Chinese Fishing Nets, colonial Fort Kochi, Jewish Synagogue, and Mattancherry Dutch Palace.

kollam.name: Kollam
kollam.description: Ancient spice seaport on Ashtamudi Lake (gateway to backwaters), Tangasseri Lighthouse, and Thangassery British-era church ruins.

kottayam.name: Kottayam
kottayam.description: City of Letters and Lakes, rubber plantation belt holding ancient Syrian Christian churches (Valiyapally) and Thazhathangady Juma Masjid.

kovalam.name: Kovalam
kovalam.description: World-famous crescent beach destination crowned by the striped red-and-white Vizhinjam Lighthouse, Hawa Beach, and Ayurvedic resorts.

thiruvananthapuram.name: Thiruvananthapuram
thiruvananthapuram.description: Capital city holding the opulent Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, Kuthiramalika Palace Museum, Napier Museum, and Kovalam coastline.

bhopal.name: Bhopal
bhopal.description: City of Lakes combining Begum architectural monuments (Taj-ul-Masajid, Shaukat Mahal), Bharat Bhavan arts center, and Upper Lake.

gwalior.name: Gwalior
gwalior.description: Historic citadel city crowned by the impregnable Gwalior Fort (Pearl in the necklace of forts), Man Singh Palace tiles, and Scindia Jai Vilas Palace.

jabalpur.name: Jabalpur
jabalpur.description: Cultural center on the Narmada featuring dramatic Marble Rocks canyon at Bhedaghat, roaring Dhuandhar waterfall, and Madan Mahal fort.

orchha.name: Orchha
orchha.description: Medieval Bundela kingdom on the boulder-strewn Betwa river featuring Jahangir Mahal palace, Ram Raja Temple (where Rama is king), and chhatris.

pachmarhi.name: Pachmarhi
pachmarhi.description: Queen of Satpura, only hill station in MP, featuring Pandava Caves, Bee Falls, Dhoopgarh sunset peak (highest in MP), and sal forests.

sanchi.name: Sanchi
sanchi.description: UNESCO World Heritage site holding the 3rd-century BCE Great Stupa commissioned by Emperor Ashoka with four exquisitely carved stone torana gates.

ujjain.name: Ujjain
ujjain.description: Ancient holy city on the Shipra River, hosting Simhastha Kumbh Mela, Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga temple, and Jantar Mantar observatory.

amravati.name: Amravati
amravati.description: Cultural capital of Vidarbha featuring the historic Ambadevi and Ekvira Devi temples and gateway to Melghat Tiger Reserve and Chikhaldara hills.

chhatrapati-sambhaji-nagar.name: Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar
chhatrapati-sambhaji-nagar.description: Tourism Capital of Maharashtra, gateway to UNESCO World Heritage Ajanta & Ellora cave complexes, Daulatabad Fort, and Bibi Ka Maqbara.

igatpuri.name: Igatpuri
igatpuri.description: Western Ghats hill station enveloped in monsoon mists, home to Vipassana International Academy (Dhamma Giri), Tringalwadi Fort, and waterfalls.

jalgaon.name: Jalgaon
jalgaon.description: Banana City and Golden City of Maharashtra, railhead gateway to the 30 rock-cut Buddhist caves of Ajanta (UNESCO).

kolhapur.name: Kolhapur
kolhapur.description: Historic Maratha kingdom on the Panchganga river famed for Mahalakshmi Ambabai Temple, New Palace museum, wrestling (Kushti), and leather chappals.

mahabaleshwar.name: Mahabaleshwar
mahabaleshwar.description: Highest hill station in the Western Ghats, strawberry capital of India, featuring Arthur's Seat cliff, Venna Lake, and Old Mahabaleshwar temple.

mumbai.name: Mumbai
mumbai.description: Financial capital of India featuring UNESCO Victorian Gothic Ensembles, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Elephanta Caves, and Gateway of India.

nagpur.name: Nagpur
nagpur.description: Winter Capital of Maharashtra, Orange City, geographic Zero Mile Stone of India, Deekshabhoomi stupa, and tiger gateway to central India.

nashik.name: Nashik
nashik.description: Wine Capital of India on the Godavari river, host of Kumbh Mela, holding Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga, Panchavati, and Pandavleni Buddhist caves.

pune.name: Pune
pune.description: Oxford of the East and Maratha cultural capital, featuring Shaniwar Wada peshwa palace, Sinhagad hilltop fort, Aga Khan Palace, and Osho Ashram.

satara.name: Satara
satara.description: Historic capital of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj guarded by Ajinkyatara fort, gateway to UNESCO World Heritage Kaas Valley of Flowers and Thoseghar waterfalls.

imphal.name: Imphal
imphal.description: Capital city holding ancient Kangla Fort, Ima Keithel (world's only women-run market), Shri Govindaji Temple, and gateway to Loktak Lake.

cherrapunjee.name: Cherrapunjee
cherrapunjee.description: Sohra — wettest place on Earth featuring dramatic Nohkalikai waterfall, Mawsmai limestone cave, and bio-engineered double-decker living root bridges.

shillong.name: Shillong
shillong.description: Scotland of the East, pine-covered hill capital featuring Ward's Lake, Elephant Falls, Don Bosco Museum of Indigenous Cultures, and Shillong Peak.

aizawl.name: Aizawl
aizawl.description: Spectacular ridge-top capital at 3,700 feet, featuring Solomon's Temple, Mizoram State Museum, Durtlang Hills, and vibrant Bara Bazar handloom market.

champhai.name: Champhai
champhai.description: Rice Bowl of Mizoram on the Myanmar border with verdant valley views, ancient monoliths at Mungmang, and heart-shaped Rih Dil lake nearby.

lunglei.name: Lunglei
lunglei.description: Second largest city of Mizoram named after a stone bridge landmark on the Nghasih stream, offering views of Tlawng river valley and Khawnglung wildlife.

serchhip.name: Serchhip
serchhip.description: Central district featuring highest literacy, spectacular Vantawng Falls (highest waterfall in Mizoram), and tranquil Thenzawl handloom village.

dimapur.name: Dimapur
dimapur.description: Commercial gateway of Nagaland holding ancient 10th-century Kachari Kingdom mushroom-domed monolith ruins, Diezephe craft village, and Triple Falls.

kohima.name: Kohima
kohima.description: Hilltop capital holding historic World War II Kohima War Cemetery (Battle of the Tennis Court), Kisama Heritage Village (Hornbill Festival), and Dzukou Valley.

mokokchung.name: Mokokchung
mokokchung.description: Cultural and intellectual heart of the Ao Naga tribe, scenic hill ridges, Longkhum eagle-view village, and traditional Moatsu festival.

bhubaneswar.name: Bhubaneswar
bhubaneswar.description: Temple City of India boasting 500+ sandstone Kalinga temples (Lingaraj, Mukteshvara, Rajarani), 1st-century BCE Udayagiri & Khandagiri Jain caves, and Dhauli.

cuttack.name: Cuttack
cuttack.description: Millennium City on the Mahanadi-Kathajodi delta, famed for the medieval 14th-century Barabati Fort, silver filigree Tarakasi crafts, and Bali Yatra.

mayurbhanj.name: Mayurbhanj
mayurbhanj.description: Royal district home to UNESCO Similipal Biosphere Reserve (tigers and waterfalls), Baripada royal palace, and acrobatic Mayurbhanj Chhau martial dance.

puri.name: Puri
puri.description: Sacred coastal Char Dham holy city centered on the 12th-century Jagannath Temple (Rath Yatra), Golden Beach (Blue Flag), and nearby Konark Sun Temple (UNESCO).

amritsar.name: Amritsar
amritsar.description: Founded in 1577 by Guru Ram Das, the fourth Sikh Guru, Amritsar is the preeminent spiritual and cultural center of the Sikh faith. It is home to Sri Harmandir Sahib (the Golden Temple), Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial, Gobindgarh Fort, and the world first Partition Museum.

patiala.name: Patiala
patiala.description: Founded in 1763 by Baba Ala Singh, Patiala was the premier princely state of Punjab. It is renowned for the mud-and-brick Qila Mubarak fortress complex, the Patiala Gharana of Hindustani music, Phulkari embroidery, and the NIS sports institute.

anandpur-sahib.name: Anandpur Sahib
anandpur-sahib.description: Nestled between the Shivalik foothills and Sutlej River, Anandpur Sahib (City of Bliss) is one of the five Takhts of Sikhism. It is renowned for Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib and the world-renowned Virasat-e-Khalsa museum designed by Moshe Safdie.

ludhiana.name: Ludhiana
ludhiana.description: Manchester of India on the Sutlej river featuring Maharaja Ranjit Singh War Museum, historic Lodhi Fort, and Punjab Agricultural University.

jaipur.name: Jaipur
jaipur.description: Founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, Jaipur was designed on Vastu Shastra principles by Vidyadhar Bhattacharya. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage City in 2019, it features Amber Fort, City Palace, Hawa Mahal, and Jantar Mantar.

udaipur.name: Udaipur
udaipur.description: Founded in 1559 by Maharana Udai Singh II, Udaipur is situated around Lake Pichola, Fateh Sagar, and Swaroop Sagar. It features the massive City Palace complex, Jag Mandir, and Saheliyon-ki-Bari.

ajmer.name: Ajmer
ajmer.description: Spiritual oasis in the Aravalli hills holding the world-renowned Sufi shrine Dargah Sharif of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra, and Taragarh Fort.

bikaner.name: Bikaner
bikaner.description: Desert citadel featuring the invincible red sandstone Junagarh Fort, Lalgarh Palace, Karni Mata rat temple at Deshnoke, and camel breeding center.

chittorgarh.name: Chittorgarh
chittorgarh.description: Symbol of Rajput chivalry, largest fort in India (UNESCO), holding Vijay Stambha (Tower of Victory), Kirti Stambha, and Queen Padmini's Palace.

jaisalmer.name: Jaisalmer
jaisalmer.description: The Golden City rising out of the Thar Desert, holding the living Sonar Qila (UNESCO Golden Fort), Patwon ki Haveli, Gadisar Lake, and Sam sand dunes.

jodhpur.name: Jodhpur
jodhpur.description: The Blue City crowned by the colossal Mehrangarh Fort rising 400 feet above the city, Umaid Bhawan Art Deco palace, and marble Jaswant Thada memorial.

mount-abu.name: Mount Abu
mount-abu.description: Only hill station in Rajasthan at 4,000 ft in the Aravallis, home to the exquisite 11th-13th century Dilwara Jain marble temples, Nakki Lake, and Guru Shikhar peak.

gangtok.name: Gangtok
gangtok.description: Scenic mountain capital perched at 5,400 ft overlooking Mt. Khangchendzonga, featuring Enchey Monastery, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, and MG Marg.

mangan.name: Mangan
mangan.description: Cardamom capital and gateway to high-altitude North Sikkim, alpine Yumthang Valley of Flowers, Gurudongmar glacial lake, and hot springs.

pelling.name: Pelling
pelling.description: Hill retreat offering closest views of Khangchendzonga, holding 1705 Pemayangtse Monastery, Rabdentse royal ruins, and Singshore suspension bridge.

chennai.name: Chennai
chennai.description: Cultural gateway of South India, featuring Marina Beach, 7th-century Kapaleeshwarar temple, British Fort St. George, and San Thome Basilica.

coimbatore.name: Coimbatore
coimbatore.description: Manchester of South India at the foothills of Nilgiris, home to the colossal Adiyogi Shiva bust statue, Marudhamalai temple, and textile museums.

kanniyakumari.name: Kanniyakumari
kanniyakumari.description: Southernmost tip of mainland India where Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean and Bay of Bengal converge, with Vivekananda Rock Memorial and Thiruvalluvar Statue.

madurai.name: Madurai
madurai.description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, soul of Tamil culture centered on the towering multi-sculptured gopurams of Meenakshi Amman Temple.

mamallapuram.name: Mamallapuram
mamallapuram.description: UNESCO World Heritage 7th-century Pallava coastal monuments including the Shore Temple, monolithic Pancha Rathas, and Descent of the Ganges rock relief.

ooty.name: Ooty
ooty.description: Queen of Hill Stations (Udhagamandalam) at 7,350 ft in the Nilgiris, terminus of UNESCO Nilgiri Mountain Toy Train, Botanical Gardens, and tea hills.

rameswaram.name: Rameswaram
rameswaram.description: Sacred Char Dham island temple town connected by Pamban Bridge, home to Ramanathaswamy Temple with world's longest pillared corridor and Dhanushkodi ghost town.

thanjavur.name: Thanjavur
thanjavur.description: Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu and Chola imperial capital holding UNESCO World Heritage Brihadisvara Temple (Big Temple), Maratha Palace, and Tanjore paintings.

tiruchirappalli.name: Tiruchirappalli
tiruchirappalli.description: Historic Cauvery river city dominated by the dramatic 83-meter high Rockfort Ucchi Pillayar Temple and colossal Ranganathaswamy Temple complex at Srirangam.

bhongir.name: Bhongir
bhongir.description: Historic town famed for the monolithic egg-shaped Bhongir Fort built by Western Chalukya ruler Tribhuvanamalla Vikramaditya VI on a single isolated rock.

hyderabad.name: Hyderabad
hyderabad.description: City of Pearls and Nizams, holding the 1591 Charminar, massive Golconda Fort with acoustic engineering, Qutb Shahi Tombs, and Salar Jung Museum.

karimnagar.name: Karimnagar
karimnagar.description: Historic town on the Manair river famed for Silver Filigree (Tarkashi) delicate jewelry, Elgandal hill fortress, and Lower Manair Dam.

khammam.name: Khammam
khammam.description: Historic town featuring the 10th-century Kakatiya stone Khammam Fort perched on Stambhadri hill, Palair lake, and gateway to Bhadrachalam temple.

warangal.name: Warangal
warangal.description: Historic Kakatiya capital holding the 12th-century Thousand Pillar Temple, Warangal Fort stone gateways (Kakatiya Kala Thoranam), and UNESCO Ramappa Temple.

agartala.name: Agartala
agartala.description: Royal capital city holding neoclassical white marble Ujjayanta Palace, water palace Neermahal on Rudrasagar Lake, and Tripura Sundari Shakti Peetha.

unakoti.name: Unakoti
unakoti.description: Ancient Shaivite pilgrimage wonder in forested hills holding massive 7th-9th century rock-carved reliefs (including 30-foot Shiva Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava).

agra.name: Agra
agra.description: Agra served as the imperial capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir, and Shah Jahan. It is home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri, along with the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah.

varanasi.name: Varanasi
varanasi.description: Known anciently as Kashi and Banaras, Varanasi stretches along the crescent-shaped western bank of the sacred river Ganga. It is home to Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, 84 historic stone ghats, and centuries-old traditions of silk weaving, Banarasi cuisine, and classical music.

ayodhya.name: Ayodhya
ayodhya.description: Sacred birthplace of Lord Rama on the holy Saryu river, holding the grand Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi fortress temple, and ancient Ram Ki Paidi ghats.

bareilly.name: Bareilly
bareilly.description: Historic Rohilkhand trade city celebrated for Zari-Zardozi embroidery, cane furniture, seven ancient Shiva Nath temples (Alakhnath, Trivatinath), and Jhumka.

jhansi.name: Jhansi
jhansi.description: Gateway to Bundelkhand and seat of legendary 1857 warrior queen Rani Lakshmibai, holding the formidable granite Jhansi Fort and Government Museum.

lucknow.name: Lucknow
lucknow.description: City of Nawabs famed for refined Tehzeeb culture, colossal gravity-defying arch of Bara Imambara (Bhulbhulaiya maze), Rumi Darwaza, and Chikankari embroidery.

mathura.name: Mathura
mathura.description: Sacred birthplace of Lord Krishna on the Yamuna river, holding Shri Krishna Janmasthan temple, Vishram Ghat aarti, and neighboring sacred Vrindavan.

prayagraj.name: Prayagraj
prayagraj.description: Triveni Sangam sacred confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and mythical Saraswati, site of the Maha Kumbh Mela, Mughal Allahabad Fort, and Anand Bhavan.

almora.name: Almora
almora.description: Cultural capital of Kumaon perched on a horse-saddle ridge, holding Bright End Corner sunset point, Kasar Devi hippie trail, and Jageshwar temple valley.

badrinath.name: Badrinath
badrinath.description: Premier Himalayan Char Dham holy shrine of Lord Vishnu on the Alaknanda River, framed by Nar and Narayana mountain ranges, Tapt Kund, and Mana village.

chamoli.name: Chamoli
chamoli.description: Himalayan district gateway to UNESCO Valley of Flowers, Hemkund Sahib high-altitude lake, Badrinath, and cradle of the historic Chipko forest movement.

haridwar.name: Haridwar
haridwar.description: Gateway to the Gods where the Ganges leaves the Himalayas, famed for Har Ki Pauri ghat evening Ganga Aarti, Mansa Devi ropeway, and Kumbh Mela.

kedarnath.name: Kedarnath
kedarnath.description: Most revered Himalayan Jyotirlinga shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, resting at 11,755 ft near Mandakini river headwaters against the Kedarnath glacier peak.

mussoorie.name: Mussoorie
mussoorie.description: Queen of the Hills at 6,500 ft, featuring Mall Road promenade, Kempty Falls, Gun Hill cable car, Lal Tibba viewpoint, and colonial heritage estates.

nainital.name: Nainital
nainital.description: Famous lake district town nestled around the emerald eye-shaped Naini Lake, Naina Devi temple, Snow View cable car, and British Governor's Raj Bhavan.

new-tehri.name: New Tehri
new-tehri.description: Planned modern hill town overlooking Tehri Dam (tallest dam in India) and massive green reservoir lake offering water sports, boating, and scenic vistas.

pithoragarh.name: Pithoragarh
pithoragarh.description: Little Kashmir in the Soar Valley, border district gateway to Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage route, Chand-era Pithoragarh Fort, and alpine meadows.

rishikesh.name: Rishikesh
rishikesh.description: Yoga Capital of the World along the turquoise Ganges, famed for Lakshman Jhula, Ram Jhula, Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia), and whitewater rafting.

uttarkashi.name: Uttarkashi
uttarkashi.description: Northern holy town on the Bhagirathi river, home to ancient Vishwanath Temple with brass trident, Nehru Institute of Mountaineering, and Gangotri base.

darjeeling.name: Darjeeling
darjeeling.description: Queen of the Hills holding the UNESCO World Heritage Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Toy Train), Tiger Hill sunrise over Kanchenjunga, and tea gardens.

durgapur.name: Durgapur
durgapur.description: Steel city on the Damodar River, planned by Joseph Allen Stein, featuring Durgapur Barrage, Troika Park, and gateway to terracotta temples of Bishnupur.

howrah.name: Howrah
howrah.description: Historic twin city to Kolkata on the Hooghly river, holding iconic cantilevered Howrah Bridge, Belur Math (Ramakrishna Mission), and Indian Botanical Garden (Great Banyan).

kolkata.name: Kolkata
kolkata.description: City of Joy and cultural capital of India, featuring Victoria Memorial, Dakshineswar Kali Temple, Indian Museum, Park Street, and Durga Puja festival (UNESCO).

siliguri.name: Siliguri
siliguri.description: Strategic transportation hub in the chicken's neck corridor, gateway to Darjeeling, Sikkim, and Bhutan, featuring Salugara Buddhist Stupa and Mahananda sanctuary.

mayabunder.name: Mayabunder
mayabunder.description: Administrative town in Middle Andaman known for Karmatang beach turtle nesting ground, mangrove creeks, and Karen Burmese settler culture.

rangat.name: Rangat
rangat.description: Eco-tourism destination in Middle Andaman boasting the Dhaninallah Mangrove Walkway (longest in India), Amkunj beach, and Cutbert Bay turtle haven.

sri-vijaya-puram.name: Sri Vijaya Puram
sri-vijaya-puram.description: Territory capital (formerly Port Blair) holding the National Memorial Cellular Jail, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Island (Ross Island), and coral beaches.

chandigarh.name: Chandigarh
chandigarh.description: The City Beautiful, planned by Le Corbusier, featuring the UNESCO World Heritage Capitol Complex, Nek Chand Rock Garden, and Sukhna Lake.

daman.name: Daman
daman.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
daman.description: Coastal Portuguese enclave on the Gulf of Khambhat featuring the 16th-century Moti Daman Fort, Church of Bom Jesus, and Devka beach.

diu.name: Diu
diu.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
diu.description: Picturesque island citadel surrounded by sea waves, holding formidable sea-facing Diu Fort, St. Paul Church, Naida Caves, and Nagoa beach.

silvassa.name: Silvassa
silvassa.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
silvassa.description: Capital of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, featuring Portuguese Church of Our Lady of Piety, Warli tribal cultural museum, and Madhuban dam reservoir.

delhi.name: Delhi
delhi.description: National Capital Territory of India featuring three UNESCO World Heritage monuments (Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Red Fort), India Gate, and Chandni Chowk.

anantnag.name: Anantnag
anantnag.description: Commercial capital of South Kashmir known for mineral water springs, 8th-century Martand Sun Temple ruins, and gateway to Amarnath Cave.

gulmarg.name: Gulmarg
gulmarg.description: Meadow of Flowers, premier winter ski resort of India, holding the world's second-highest operating cable car (Gulmarg Gondola to Apharwat peak at 13,780 ft).

jammu.name: Jammu
jammu.description: City of Temples and winter capital on the Tawi River, holding historic Bahu Fort, Raghunath Temple, Amar Mahal palace museum, and gateway to Vaishno Devi.

pahalgam.name: Pahalgam
pahalgam.description: Valley of the Shepherds on the Lidder River, starting point for the annual Amarnath Yatra, featuring Betaab Valley, Aru Valley, and Baisaran meadow.

patnitop.name: Patnitop
patnitop.description: Picturesque pine-forested plateau at 6,640 ft along the Jammu-Srinagar highway, Skyview cable car ropeway, Sanasar Lake, and Nag Temple.

srinagar.name: Srinagar
srinagar.description: Summer capital situated in the heart of Kashmir Valley, world-famous for Dal Lake houseboats and shikaras, Mughal Pleasure Gardens, and wooden Jama Masjid.

kargil.name: Kargil
kargil.description: Historic transit city on the Suru river, holding the Kargil War Memorial at Dras, ancient Rock-cut Maitreya Buddha at Mulbekh, and gateway to Zanskar.

leh.name: Leh
leh.description: Capital of Ladakh at 11,500 ft, featuring the 9-storey 17th-century Leh Palace, white Shanti Stupa, Hemis & Thiksey monasteries, and Khardung La pass.

kavaratti.name: Kavaratti
kavaratti.description: Capital of Lakshadweep territory, an idyllic coral atoll with crystal-clear turquoise lagoons, marine aquarium, and 17th-century carved wooden Ujra Mosque.

puducherry.name: Puducherry
puducherry.description: French Riviera of the East, famed for French Quarter (White Town) colonial architecture, Sri Aurobindo Ashram, Promenade Beach, and experimental township Auroville.

taj-mahal.name: Taj Mahal
taj-mahal.summary: 17th-century white marble mausoleum built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, universally admired as an eternal jewel of Muslim art in India.
taj-mahal.description: 17th-century white marble mausoleum built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, universally admired as an eternal jewel of Muslim art in India.
taj-mahal.history: Commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of Mumtaz Mahal. Universally admired as an eternal symbol of devotion and the pinnacle of Mughal aesthetic symmetry.

fatehpur-sikri.name: Fatehpur Sikri City of Victory
fatehpur-sikri.summary: Walled royal capital built by Emperor Akbar featuring Buland Darwaza, Panch Mahal, and the white marble Tomb of Salim Chishti.

qutub-minar.summary: World's tallest brick minaret at 72.5 meters surrounded by ancient funerary and ceremonial monuments, including the 4th-century rust-resistant Iron Pillar.
qutub-minar.description: World's tallest brick minaret at 72.5 meters surrounded by ancient funerary and ceremonial monuments, including the 4th-century rust-resistant Iron Pillar.

red-fort.summary: Massive red sandstone citadel served as the seat of the Mughal Empire for nearly 200 years and the traditional venue for the national Independence Day address.

humayuns-tomb.name: Humayun's Tomb
humayuns-tomb.summary: The first monumental garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent, establishing the architectural prototype that culminated in the Taj Mahal.
humayuns-tomb.description: The first monumental garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent, establishing the architectural prototype that culminated in the Taj Mahal.

india-gate.summary: 42-meter-high triumphal arch honoring over 84,000 soldiers, standing at the eastern terminal of Kartavya Path with the adjoining National War Memorial.

india-gate.history: Commemorates soldiers of the British Indian Army who lost their lives in the First World War and Third Anglo-Afghan War, inscribed with over 13,000 names.

golden-temple-amritsar.name: Sri Harmandir Sahib (The Golden Temple)
golden-temple-amritsar.summary: The holiest gurdwara of Sikhism surrounded by the holy Amrit Sarovar, famed for spiritual harmony and the world's largest free community kitchen (Langar).
golden-temple-amritsar.description: The holiest gurdwara of Sikhism surrounded by the holy Amrit Sarovar, famed for spiritual harmony and the world's largest free community kitchen (Langar).
golden-temple-amritsar.history: Fifth Sikh Guru, Guru Arjan Dev Ji, designed the gurdwara with four entrances welcoming people of all castes, and installed the Adi Granth in 1604.

kalka-shimla-railway.name: Kalka-Shimla Mountain Railway
kalka-shimla-railway.summary: Historic 96-km narrow-gauge railway climbing through 102 tunnels and over 800 stone arch bridges from the Himalayan foothills to Shimla.
kalka-shimla-railway.description: Historic 96-km narrow-gauge railway climbing through 102 tunnels and over 800 stone arch bridges from the Himalayan foothills to Shimla.
kalka-shimla-railway.history: Constructed under severe Himalayan terrain constraints to connect British India's summer capital; Baba Bhalku guided tunnel alignments using his stick.

kedarnath-temple.name: Kedarnath Temple
kedarnath-temple.summary: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva standing at 3,584m altitude against the towering snowbound Kedarnath peak in the Garhwal Himalayas.
kedarnath-temple.description: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva standing at 3,584m altitude against the towering snowbound Kedarnath peak in the Garhwal Himalayas.
kedarnath-temple.history: Confounded modern structural engineers by surviving the catastrophic 2013 Himalayan deluge thanks to its massive interlocking stone foundation.

shalimar-bagh-srinagar.name: Shalimar Bagh Mughal Garden
shalimar-bagh-srinagar.summary: Royal Mughal garden terraced across Dal Lake, built by Jahangir for Nur Jahan with black marble pavilions, fountains, and towering chinar trees.
shalimar-bagh-srinagar.description: Royal Mughal garden terraced across Dal Lake, built by Jahangir for Nur Jahan with black marble pavilions, fountains, and towering chinar trees.
shalimar-bagh-srinagar.history: Celebrated by Emperor Jahangir with his famed verse: 'Gar Firdaus bar-rue zamin ast, hamin ast-o hamin ast-o hamin ast' (If paradise is on earth, it is here).
shalimar-bagh-srinagar.heritage_status: ASI Protected Heritage Garden (UNESCO Tentative List)

leh-palace.name: Leh Palace & Tsemo Fort
leh-palace.summary: Nine-storey royal citadel towering over Leh Old Town modeled after Lhasa's Potala Palace, offering sweeping panoramic views of the Zanskar range.
leh-palace.description: Nine-storey royal citadel towering over Leh Old Town modeled after Lhasa's Potala Palace, offering sweeping panoramic views of the Zanskar range.
leh-palace.history: Built by King Sengge Namgyal as the royal residence of the Namgyal dynasty until the Dogra invasion in the mid-19th century.

capitol-complex-chandigarh.name: The Capitol Complex (Le Corbusier)
capitol-complex-chandigarh.summary: Masterpiece of 20th-century modern architecture comprising the Secretariat, High Court, Legislative Assembly, and the iconic 26-meter Open Hand Monument.
capitol-complex-chandigarh.description: Masterpiece of 20th-century modern architecture comprising the Secretariat, High Court, Legislative Assembly, and the iconic 26-meter Open Hand Monument.
capitol-complex-chandigarh.history: Commissioned by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as a city unfettered by existing traditions, symbolizing a newly independent democratic India.

amber-fort.name: Amber Fort & Palace (Amer)
amber-fort.summary: Hilltop citadel overlooking Maota Lake, famous for the glittering Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) and majestic Rajput courtyards.
amber-fort.description: Hilltop citadel overlooking Maota Lake, famous for the glittering Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) and majestic Rajput courtyards.

bandra-fort.summary: 17th-century Portuguese watchtower fort overlooking Mahim Bay and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link.
bandra-fort.description: Bandra Fort, officially Castella de Aguada (Fort of the Waterpoint), is a historic Portuguese watchtower fortress erected in 1640 at Land's End in Bandra. It commands sweeping coastal views over Mahim Bay to the south and the Arabian Sea to the west.
bandra-fort.history: Built by the Portuguese as a strategic lookout point along the sea route, later held by the Marathas and the British East India Company.
bandra-fort.detailed_description: Built by the Portuguese as a strategic lookout point along the sea route, later held by the Marathas and the British East India Company.
bandra-fort.short_description: 17th-century Portuguese watchtower fort overlooking Mahim Bay and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link.

colaba-causeway.name: Colaba Causeway
colaba-causeway.summary: Vibrant commercial and cultural boulevard famous for street markets, vintage cafes, and colonial charm.
colaba-causeway.description: Colaba Causeway (officially Shahid Bhagat Singh Road) is a bustling commercial thoroughfare in South Mumbai connecting Colaba and the Old Woman's Island. It is renowned for its eclectic street shopping, handicraft stalls, heritage boutiques, and vintage establishments like Cafe Mondegar and Leopold Cafe.
colaba-causeway.history: Constructed by the British East India Company in 1838 to bridge the tidal waters between the islands of Colaba and Bombay.
colaba-causeway.detailed_description: Constructed by the British East India Company in 1838 to bridge the tidal waters between the islands of Colaba and Bombay.
colaba-causeway.short_description: Vibrant commercial and cultural boulevard famous for street markets, vintage cafes, and colonial charm.

thar-desert-sam-dunes.name: Thar Desert & Sam Sand Dunes
thar-desert-sam-dunes.summary: The Great Indian Desert featuring golden rolling ripples, camel safaris, starlit camping, and desert wildlife.
thar-desert-sam-dunes.description: The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, spans western Rajasthan with rolling golden sand dunes at Sam and Khuri near Jaisalmer. Visitors experience sweeping dune crests, cultural desert camping, Rajasthani folk dance (Kalbelia and Ghoomar), camel rides, and Desert National Park with the Great Indian Bustard.
thar-desert-sam-dunes.history: Ancient geopolitical trade crossway along historic silk routes and camel caravan tracks connecting Rajput kingdoms with Sindh and Persia.
thar-desert-sam-dunes.visiting_hours: Open 24 Hours (Camel & Jeep safaris best at sunrise 06:00 AM & sunset 05:00 PM)
thar-desert-sam-dunes.detailed_description: A popular desert landscape for camel rides, dune views, and cultural camps.
thar-desert-sam-dunes.short_description: A popular desert landscape for camel rides, dune views, and cultural camps.
thar-desert-sam-dunes.opening_hours: Usually daytime; timings vary by attraction

lonavala-tigers-point.name: Tiger's Point (Tiger's Leap)
lonavala-tigers-point.summary: Dramatic 650-meter cliff-top viewpoint resembling a leaping tiger into the valley, famous for echo point and rolling Sahyadri clouds.
lonavala-tigers-point.description: Perched high above the valley in Kurvande near Lonavala, Tiger's Leap offers stunning sheer drop views of the Western Ghats, waterfalls, and mist-covered mountain valleys.
lonavala-tigers-point.detailed_description: Dramatic 650-meter cliff-top viewpoint resembling a leaping tiger into the valley, famous for echo point and rolling Sahyadri clouds.
lonavala-tigers-point.short_description: Dramatic 650-meter cliff-top viewpoint resembling a leaping tiger into the valley, famous for echo point and rolling Sahyadri clouds.

lonavala-bhushi-dam.name: Bhushi Dam & Cascades
lonavala-bhushi-dam.summary: Historic 1860s masonry dam on the Indrayani River, world-famous for its stepped waterfalls and gushing monsoon cascades.
lonavala-bhushi-dam.description: Constructed in the late 1860s for the Great Indian Peninsula Railway to supply water to steam locomotives, Bhushi Dam is Lonavala's most beloved monsoon tourist hotspot.
lonavala-bhushi-dam.detailed_description: Historic 1860s masonry dam on the Indrayani River, world-famous for its stepped waterfalls and gushing monsoon cascades.
lonavala-bhushi-dam.short_description: Historic 1860s masonry dam on the Indrayani River, world-famous for its stepped waterfalls and gushing monsoon cascades.

lonavala-karla-caves.name: Karla Caves (Grand Chaitya Hall)
lonavala-karla-caves.summary: Ancient 2nd-century BCE rock-cut Buddhist shrine with India's largest Chaitya hall, original 2,200-year-old teak wood ribs and lion pillars.
lonavala-karla-caves.description: An archaeological marvel carved into the rocky hill at Karli, Karla Caves house the largest early Buddhist rock-cut prayer hall in India with 37 majestic octagonal pillars and the sacred Ekvira Temple.
lonavala-karla-caves.detailed_description: Ancient 2nd-century BCE rock-cut Buddhist shrine with India's largest Chaitya hall, original 2,200-year-old teak wood ribs and lion pillars.
lonavala-karla-caves.short_description: Ancient 2nd-century BCE rock-cut Buddhist shrine with India's largest Chaitya hall, original 2,200-year-old teak wood ribs and lion pillars.

lonavala-bhaja-caves.name: Bhaja Caves & Waterfall
lonavala-bhaja-caves.summary: Group of 22 rock-cut Buddhist caves from 2nd century BCE featuring wooden architecture carvings, a dancing woman relief, and 14 stupas.
lonavala-bhaja-caves.description: Perched 400 feet above the village of Bhaja near Lonavala, this monastic complex features extraordinary Buddhist reliefs, ancient Hinayana stupas, and a seasonal monsoon waterfall cascade.
lonavala-bhaja-caves.detailed_description: Group of 22 rock-cut Buddhist caves from 2nd century BCE featuring wooden architecture carvings, a dancing woman relief, and 14 stupas.
lonavala-bhaja-caves.short_description: Group of 22 rock-cut Buddhist caves from 2nd century BCE featuring wooden architecture carvings, a dancing woman relief, and 14 stupas.

lonavala-lohagad-fort.name: Lohagad Fort (The Iron Fortress)
lonavala-lohagad-fort.summary: Historic Maratha hilltop fortress at 1,033m elevation, fortified by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, featuring the famous Vinchukata spur.
lonavala-lohagad-fort.description: Lohagad (Iron Fort) divides the Indrayani and Pavana basins. It has four formidable gates—Ganesh Darwaja, Narayan Darwaja, Hanuman Darwaja, and Maha Darwaja—and the iconic 1,500m scorpion-tail fortified ridge.
lonavala-lohagad-fort.detailed_description: Historic Maratha hilltop fortress at 1,033m elevation, fortified by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, featuring the famous Vinchukata spur.
lonavala-lohagad-fort.short_description: Historic Maratha hilltop fortress at 1,033m elevation, fortified by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, featuring the famous Vinchukata spur.

khandala-rajmachi-fort.name: Rajmachi Fort & Sahyadri Plateau
khandala-rajmachi-fort.summary: Historic twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) guarding the ancient Borghat pass, famous for lush trekking, views, and fireflies.
khandala-rajmachi-fort.description: Standing strategically in the rugged Sahyadri mountains between Khandala and Karjat, Rajmachi Fort comprises two citadel fortresses offering breathtaking vistas of the Ulhas river valley and Duke's Nose.
khandala-rajmachi-fort.detailed_description: Historic twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) guarding the ancient Borghat pass, famous for lush trekking, views, and fireflies.
khandala-rajmachi-fort.short_description: Historic twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) guarding the ancient Borghat pass, famous for lush trekking, views, and fireflies.

khandala-dukes-nose.name: Duke's Nose (Nagphani Peak)
khandala-dukes-nose.summary: Dramatic cliff peak shaped like a cobra's hood offering thrilling rock climbing, rappelling, and 360-degree Sahyadri valley views.
khandala-dukes-nose.description: Also known as Nagphani due to its resemblance to a cobra's raised hood, the peak was nicknamed Duke's Nose by British surveyors. It is renowned for its sheer vertical drop and sweeping views of the Khandala ghats.
khandala-dukes-nose.detailed_description: Dramatic cliff peak shaped like a cobra's hood offering thrilling rock climbing, rappelling, and 360-degree Sahyadri valley views.
khandala-dukes-nose.short_description: Dramatic cliff peak shaped like a cobra's hood offering thrilling rock climbing, rappelling, and 360-degree Sahyadri valley views.

khandala-sunset-point.name: Khandala Sunset Point (Amrutanjan Ghat)
khandala-sunset-point.summary: Celebrated scenic vantage point over the deep Bhor Ghat valley and Duke's Nose, famous for spectacular sunsets and cloud phenomena.
khandala-sunset-point.description: Located near the historic Amrutanjan Bridge on the old Mumbai-Pune highway, this iconic viewpoint provides expansive vistas of lush valleys, train tunnels cutting through mountains, and golden sunsets.
khandala-sunset-point.detailed_description: Celebrated scenic vantage point over the deep Bhor Ghat valley and Duke's Nose, famous for spectacular sunsets and cloud phenomena.
khandala-sunset-point.short_description: Celebrated scenic vantage point over the deep Bhor Ghat valley and Duke's Nose, famous for spectacular sunsets and cloud phenomena.

khandala-kune-waterfalls.name: Kune Waterfalls (Three-Tier Cascade)
khandala-kune-waterfalls.summary: India's 14th highest waterfall dropping 200 meters in three majestic tiers amid dense Sahyadri greenery.
khandala-kune-waterfalls.description: Nestled in the lush greenery between Khandala and Lonavala, Kune Falls plunges 660 feet into a rocky basin against the backdrop of the Sahyadri mountains, creating an unforgettable monsoon spectacle.
khandala-kune-waterfalls.detailed_description: India's 14th highest waterfall dropping 200 meters in three majestic tiers amid dense Sahyadri greenery.
khandala-kune-waterfalls.short_description: India's 14th highest waterfall dropping 200 meters in three majestic tiers amid dense Sahyadri greenery.

lonavala-lions-point.name: Lion's Point Viewpoint
lonavala-lions-point.summary: High-altitude vantage point between Bhushi Dam and Aamby Valley, known for soaring wind currents and panoramic mountain gorges.
lonavala-lions-point.description: Situated midway between Bhushi Dam and Aamby Valley, Lion's Point offers sharp cliff drops, winds that lift water droplets upwards, and incredible sunrise and sunset vistas across the Sahyadri range.
lonavala-lions-point.detailed_description: High-altitude vantage point between Bhushi Dam and Aamby Valley, known for soaring wind currents and panoramic mountain gorges.
lonavala-lions-point.short_description: High-altitude vantage point between Bhushi Dam and Aamby Valley, known for soaring wind currents and panoramic mountain gorges.

lonavala-pawna-lake.name: Pawna Lake & Dam Reserve
lonavala-pawna-lake.summary: Expansive freshwater reservoir framed by Lohagad, Tikona and Tung forts; premier destination for lakeside camping and kayaking.
lonavala-pawna-lake.description: Surrounded by historic Maratha fortresses, Pawna Lake offers calm waters, picturesque lakeside campsites, bonfire evenings, and water sports just 20 km from central Lonavala.
lonavala-pawna-lake.detailed_description: Expansive freshwater reservoir framed by Lohagad, Tikona and Tung forts; premier destination for lakeside camping and kayaking.
lonavala-pawna-lake.short_description: Expansive freshwater reservoir framed by Lohagad, Tikona and Tung forts; premier destination for lakeside camping and kayaking.

lonavala-celebrity-wax-museum.name: Sunil's Celebrity Wax Museum
lonavala-celebrity-wax-museum.summary: Pioneering Indian wax museum housing lifelike statues of historic leaders, scientists, freedom fighters, and cricket icons.
lonavala-celebrity-wax-museum.description: Founded by wax sculptor Sunil Kandalloor, this popular indoor museum features detailed life-size figures of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, Mahatma Gandhi, and global figures.
lonavala-celebrity-wax-museum.detailed_description: Pioneering Indian wax museum housing lifelike statues of historic leaders, scientists, freedom fighters, and cricket icons.
lonavala-celebrity-wax-museum.short_description: Pioneering Indian wax museum housing lifelike statues of historic leaders, scientists, freedom fighters, and cricket icons.

calangute-baga-beach.name: Calangute & Baga Beach
calangute-baga-beach.summary: The 'Queen of Beaches' renowned for golden sands, parasailing, beach shacks, and vibrant coastal nightlife.
calangute-baga-beach.description: Stretching along the Arabian Sea in North Goa, Calangute and Baga form Goa's most celebrated coastal strip. Famous for thrilling watersports (parasailing, jet-skiing, banana rides), sun loungers, seafood shacks serving Goan fish curry, and legendary beach clubs like Tito's and Mambos along Baga Creek.
calangute-baga-beach.history: Discovered by hippies in the late 1960s, transformed into India's premier beach tourism destination while retaining traditional Goan fishing villages nearby.
calangute-baga-beach.visiting_hours: Open 24 Hours (Watersports: 09:00 AM - 05:30 PM; Shacks open till late night)

palolem-beach.name: Palolem Beach & Crescent Bay
palolem-beach.summary: Scenic white-sand crescent bay lined with leaning coconut palms, calm turquoise waters, and dolphin cruises.
palolem-beach.description: Tucked away in Canacona in pristine South Goa, Palolem is celebrated for its natural semi-circular crescent bay framed by wooded headlands. Its gentle, shallow waters make it one of the safest beaches for swimming and sea-kayaking to Butterfly Beach and Monkey Island.
palolem-beach.history: Historically a serene Konkan fishing settlement; gained international fame for silent noise head-phone parties and wellness retreats.

fort-aguada-goa.name: Fort Aguada & Lighthouse
fort-aguada-goa.summary: 17th-century Portuguese fortress and 4-storey lighthouse standing proudly on Sinquerim Beach overlooking the Arabian Sea.
fort-aguada-goa.description: Constructed in 1612 to protect Portuguese maritime trade routes against Dutch fleets and the Marathas, Fort Aguada features formidable laterite stone ramparts and an enormous freshwater cistern ('Aguada' means watering place in Portuguese) that supplied fresh water to merchant ships.
fort-aguada-goa.history: Built in 1612 during Portuguese rule under King Philip II. It mounted 79 cannons and possessed one of Asia's earliest 19th-century light towers.

alleppey-backwaters.name: Alleppey Backwaters
alleppey-backwaters.summary: Serene network of brackish lagoons, lakes, and canals known for houseboat cruises.
alleppey-backwaters.description: Alleppey (Alappuzha) is famous for its serene backwaters, palm-fringed canals, and traditional houseboat stays in southern India.
alleppey-backwaters.history: Known as the Venice of the East, a historic maritime trading port for coir, black pepper, and spices.

pangong-tso-lake.name: Pangong Tso Lake
pangong-tso-lake.summary: World's highest endorheic saltwater lake at 4,225m altitude, famed for shifting colors from turquoise to deep azure.
pangong-tso-lake.description: Stretching over 134 km across India and Tibet, Pangong Tso is one of the most mesmerizing high-altitude natural wonders on earth. Situated at 4,225 meters (13,862 ft) above sea level in the Changthang region of Ladakh, the lake is famous for its crystal clear, hypersaline waters that change hues from brilliant aquamarine to deep indigo depending on the sun's angle.
pangong-tso-lake.history: Formed in ancient geological eras during the rise of the Himalayas. The lake has been an international borderland and an ancient pastoral corridor for Changpa nomadic yak herders.

nubra-valley-hunder.name: Nubra Valley & Hunder Sand Dunes
nubra-valley-hunder.summary: High-altitude desert valley with white sand dunes, double-humped Bactrian camels, and Diskit Gompa.
nubra-valley-hunder.description: Known historically as Ldumra ('Valley of Flowers'), Nubra Valley is a dramatic high-altitude desert wonderland carved by the Shyok and Nubra rivers. At Hunder, high-altitude sand dunes sit flanked by snow-capped Himalayan ranges, where rare double-humped Bactrian camels roam—living relics of the ancient Silk Route.
nubra-valley-hunder.history: Nubra was an indispensable juncture on the Silk Road connecting Central Asia, Yarkand, and India across the Khardung La Pass (5,359m).
nubra-valley-hunder.visiting_hours: Open 24 Hours (Camel safaris operate 08:00 AM - 06:30 PM)

shanti-stupa-leh.name: Shanti Stupa
shanti-stupa-leh.summary: White-domed Buddhist Chorten perched atop Changspa hill inaugurated by the 14th Dalai Lama.
shanti-stupa-leh.description: Constructed between 1983 and 1991 by Japanese Buddhist Bhikshu Gyomyo Nakamura and Ladakhi Buddhists as part of the Peace Pagoda mission, Shanti Stupa is a brilliant white-domed stupa holding relics of the Buddha. It provides unhindered 360-degree views of Leh town, the Indus valley, and the rugged Zanskar mountain range.
shanti-stupa-leh.history: Inaugurated in August 1991 by His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, to promote world peace, interfaith harmony, and commemorate 2,500 years of Buddhism.

magnetic-hill-ladakh.name: Magnetic Hill
magnetic-hill-ladakh.summary: Fascinating gravity-defying optical illusion hill on the Leh-Kargil National Highway.
magnetic-hill-ladakh.description: Located 30 km from Leh along the Srinagar-Leh Highway (NH 1), the Magnetic Hill is a world-famous natural curiosity. Due to the layout of the surrounding mountainous horizon, an optical illusion is created where a gentle downward slope appears to be an uphill incline, causing vehicles in neutral gear to apparently roll uphill against gravity at speeds of up to 20 km/h.
magnetic-hill-ladakh.history: Known in local folklore for generations and marked officially by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) with a designated observation box on the highway.

sonamarg-himalayas.name: Himalayas Mountain in Sonamarg
sonamarg-himalayas.summary: Majestic Himalayan mountain massif, Thajiwas Glacier, and alpine flower valleys along the Sindh River.
sonamarg-himalayas.description: Sonamarg, known poetically as the 'Meadow of Gold', sits at an elevation of 2,800 meters in the Ganderbal district of Jammu and Kashmir. Dominated by dramatic glaciated Himalayan peaks, alpine conifers, and the roaring Sindh River, it serves as the historic gateway to Ladakh across the Zoji La pass and a premier mountaineering and trekking sanctuary.
sonamarg-himalayas.history: Historically a vital trade passway on the ancient Silk Route between Kashmir, Ladakh, and Central Asia. The snowfields and Thajiwas Glacier have attracted Himalayan explorers, botanists, and nature pilgrims for centuries.
sonamarg-himalayas.visiting_hours: Open 24 Hours (Daylight hours recommended for mountain treks)

dal-lake-srinagar.name: Dal Lake & Shikara Rides
dal-lake-srinagar.summary: Iconic urban lake with handcrafted carved wooden houseboats, floating vegetable markets, and Shikara rides.
dal-lake-srinagar.description: Covering 18 square kilometers, Dal Lake is celebrated as the 'Jewel in the Crown of Kashmir'. Encircled by the Zabarwan mountain range and Mughal gardens, its tranquil waters are home to historic cedar houseboats, floating gardens (Radh), and traditional gondola-style Shikaras.
dal-lake-srinagar.history: Ancient texts name it Mahasarit. During the Mughal era in the 16th and 17th centuries, Emperor Jahangir and Nur Jahan laid out sprawling terraced pleasure gardens along its banks, while the British built ornate cedar houseboats during the colonial period.
dal-lake-srinagar.detailed_description: Famous lake known for houseboats, shikaras, floating gardens and Himalayan views.
dal-lake-srinagar.short_description: Famous lake known for houseboats, shikaras, floating gardens and Himalayan views.
dal-lake-srinagar.best_time_to_visit: March to October for general sightseeing; winter is suitable for snow activities in selected mountain destinations.
dal-lake-srinagar.opening_hours: Varies by place; check official timings before visiting.

gulmarg-gondola.name: Gulmarg Gondola & Apharwat Peak
gulmarg-gondola.summary: Asia's highest cable car system reaching 3,980 meters on Mount Apharwat with premier ski slopes.
gulmarg-gondola.description: Gulmarg ('Meadow of Flowers') is India's premier high-altitude ski resort. The Gulmarg Gondola carries passengers in two phases from the bowl of Gulmarg pine forests up to Kongdoori and onward to Mount Apharwat peak, offering breath-taking vistas of Nanga Parbat and the Pir Panjal range.
gulmarg-gondola.history: Originally named Gaurimarg by shepherd communities, it was renamed Gulmarg by Sultan Yusuf Shah in the 16th century, captivated by its wild flowers. The modern French-built ropeway was completed between 1998 and 2005.
gulmarg-gondola.detailed_description: Popular mountain destination known for meadows, skiing and the Gulmarg Gondola.
gulmarg-gondola.short_description: Popular mountain destination known for meadows, skiing and the Gulmarg Gondola.
gulmarg-gondola.best_time_to_visit: March to October for general sightseeing; winter is suitable for snow activities in selected mountain destinations.
gulmarg-gondola.opening_hours: Varies by place; check official timings before visiting.

betaab-valley-pahalgam.name: Betaab Valley & Baisaran Valley
betaab-valley-pahalgam.summary: Verdant Himalayan valley along the Lidder River surrounded by snow-capped peaks and deodar forests.
betaab-valley-pahalgam.description: Betaab Valley, named after the iconic Bollywood movie filmed here, is situated 15 km from Pahalgam on the way to the Amarnath Cave shrine. Framed by towering Pir Panjal peaks, weeping willows, and the crystal-clear turquoise waters of the Lidder River, it is known alongside Baisaran as Kashmir's 'Mini Switzerland'.
betaab-valley-pahalgam.history: Historically part of the sacred pilgrimage corridor to Amarnath and a pastoral pastureland for Himalayan shepherds.
betaab-valley-pahalgam.detailed_description: Picturesque valley with green meadows, streams and mountain scenery.
betaab-valley-pahalgam.short_description: Picturesque valley with green meadows, streams and mountain scenery.
betaab-valley-pahalgam.best_time_to_visit: March to October for general sightseeing; winter is suitable for snow activities in selected mountain destinations.
betaab-valley-pahalgam.opening_hours: Varies by place; check official timings before visiting.

shankaracharya-temple.name: Shankaracharya Temple
shankaracharya-temple.summary: Ancient 9th-century Shiva temple perched 1,000 feet atop Gopadari Hill overlooking Srinagar and Dal Lake.
shankaracharya-temple.description: Perched dramatically on the Shankaracharya Hill (Takht-e-Suleiman), this solid stone temple dedicated to Lord Shiva dates back in its current form to the 9th century CE. It is associated with the great philosopher Adi Shankaracharya who visited the shrine during his travels.
shankaracharya-temple.history: Believed to be founded by King Gopaditya in the 4th century BCE and renovated in the 9th century by King Lalitaditya. Adi Shankaracharya stayed here and composed the famous hymn Saundarya Lahari.
shankaracharya-temple.detailed_description: Hilltop Hindu temple offering panoramic views over Srinagar and Dal Lake.
shankaracharya-temple.short_description: Hilltop Hindu temple offering panoramic views over Srinagar and Dal Lake.
shankaracharya-temple.best_time_to_visit: March to October for general sightseeing; winter is suitable for snow activities in selected mountain destinations.

bahu-fort-jammu.name: Bahu Fort & Bagh-e-Bahu
bahu-fort-jammu.summary: Historic 3,000-year-old fortress overlooking the Tawi River housing the sacred Bawe Wali Mata shrine.
bahu-fort-jammu.description: The oldest surviving monument in Jammu city, Bahu Fort stands on a high rocky cliff on the left bank of the Tawi River. Inside the fort is the revered temple of Goddess Kali (Bawe Wali Mata), and below it lies Bagh-e-Bahu, an expansive terraced garden modeled on Mughal waterways with India's largest underground aquarium.
bahu-fort-jammu.history: Originally constructed by Raja Bahu Lochan around 3,000 years ago, and rebuilt in sandstone and lime by the Dogra rulers during the 19th and 20th centuries.
bahu-fort-jammu.detailed_description: Historic hilltop fort overlooking the Tawi River and surrounding Jammu city.
bahu-fort-jammu.short_description: Historic hilltop fort overlooking the Tawi River and surrounding Jammu city.
